Subject: NexaHealth — Post-call recap & next steps (integration + routing)

Hi Samira / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate the detailed walkthrough of the triage and clinical-search use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same page: 

Summary of needs:
- SDK integration into your backend (Node + Python) for both chat and reranking flows
- Auth: service-to-service keys with per-route scopes; team also wants region-aware routing (US primary, EU fallback for EU patients)
- Structured output / tool-calling for extraction of diagnosis codes into your EHR pipeline
- Embeddings + reranker for note search (keep vector store on your side; Redwood to provide embeddings API with batching)
- Model routing & policy: low-latency clinical prompts should prefer smaller verified models with strict token limits; high-quality summarization can route to larger models with higher cost tolerance; fallback chains when capacity constrained

Attachments: I attached a rough architecture draft and an integration checklist to get started.

Proposed next steps (owner):
1) Dev to share a model-routing example and auth recommendations (Dev) — target: EOD today
2) NexaHealth to confirm compliance constraints for EU data routing (Samira) — target: 2/20
3) Schedule technical pairing session for SDK/auth (30–45m) — Marissa to propose slots
4) We’ll provide a sample prompt set & initial eval plan for reranker quality monitoring (Neha)

If that looks right I’ll schedule a follow-up tech call for Friday morning PT.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole

Subject: RE: NexaHealth — Post-call recap & next steps (integration + routing)

Great call — adding a few concrete options on the integration and model-routing side so you can pick what fits Nexa’s constraints. I attached a small YAML that shows an example routing policy. High-level notes below.

SDK / auth:
- SDKs: we provide official Node and Python SDKs with streaming and embeddings helpers. Example initialization: 
  - Node: const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, region: 'us' })
- Auth: recommend service keys scoped to routes (e.g., embeddings:read, rerank:write). For extra security we can do mTLS or short-lived OAuth tokens via your auth server; tradeoff is complexity vs rotation safety.

Model routing & policies (example):
- Route: /v1/generate/clinical-short -> prefer: rdl-mini-clinical-1 (latency SLO 150ms), fallback: rdl-med-1, cost-threshold: $0.0008/token
- Route: /v1/generate/summaries -> prefer: rdl-std-2, fallback: rdl-llm-1 (higher quality, higher cost)
- Fallback chain behavior: if preferred model is unavailable due to capacity we try next compatible variant; if region mismatch (EU patient row) we route to EU-verified variants only
- Regional routing: header x-patient-region: EU triggers route with region priority list [eu, us] and data residency policy applied

Caching & batching:
- We’ll enable prefix caching for identical clinical prompts (session-based keys) and automatic request batching for embeddings calls (batch window 20ms by default).

Observability & quality monitoring:
- Token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, and a prompt set-based quality monitor that can trigger regression alerts.

Attached: model-routing-example.yaml (sample policy + route definitions).

Let me know if you want us to wire up a short-lived test key and a sandbox routing config for you to try. Happy to jump on the pairing session.

— Dev
Dev Patel

Thanks Marissa & Dev — this is really helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we lock in a pairing session:

1) For EU patients we need all inference to occur in EU data centers and logs retained per our retention policy (30 days). Does Redwood support per-route retention overrides?
2) On the embeddings side: we want to keep vectors in our VPC-based store. Will your embeddings API allow us to batch and still avoid sending raw notes to Redwood? We can pre-tokenize or send only hash pointers if necessary.
3) Can you confirm the expected latency for the rdl-mini-clinical-1 model at 512 tokens? The team needs to validate it meets our 150ms p95 SLO.

We’re available for a pairing session Friday 20th between 9–11 PT. Proposed agenda: quick SDK walk-through (20m), model-routing YAML review (15m), auth and keys (10m), next steps & milestones (5m).

— Samira
Director of Product Integrations | NexaHealth
samira.k@nexahealth.com

Samira — thanks for the questions. Short answers below and I’ll make sure Dev/Neha bring details to the pairing session Friday at 9:30 PT (I’ll send the invite).

1) Retention: Yes — Redwood supports per-route retention policies at the control-plane level; we can set EU routes to 30d retention and disable logs storage for routed EU inference. We’ll include the retention config in the sandbox routing YAML.

2) Embeddings: You can host vectors in your VPC store. Our embeddings endpoint supports hashed payloads and partial pre-tokenization patterns; we can batch on your side and use our batching hints to keep roundtrips efficient without storing raw notes. We’ll add an example flow to the Drive folder.

3) rdl-mini-clinical-1 latency: On current dedicated infra we see ~120ms median, ~140ms p95 at 512 tokens in our benchmarks (US region). We’ll provide a short-load test in the sandbox to validate on Nexa’s traffic pattern and report back.
